ঢাকায় তৈরি মসলিন, উনিশ শতক–বিশ শতকের প্র: Muslin made in Dhaka, nineteenth to early twentieth century. Collection:
একসময় বাংলার এক অসাধারণ সূক্ষ্ম কাপড় পরি: An exceptionally fine fabric from Bengal was once known as “woven air.” Dhakai muslin’s reputation travelled from the Mughal court to European aristocratic society. After many years, efforts are underway in Bangladesh to bring this heritage back to life. Researchers and artisans are working to revive muslin through research on phuti karpas cotton, cotton cultivation, fine spinning, and weaving.
ঢাকা ও আশপাশের অঞ্চলে তৈরি অতি সূক্ষ্ম স: Dhakai muslin was famous for the exceptionally fine cotton cloth made in and around Dhaka. Some delicate, translucent varieties had poetic names such as “ab-i-rawan,” or flowing water, and “shabnam,” or dew. This fineness depended on the quality of cotton, the skills of spinners, the long experience of weavers, and knowledge of working with local weather conditions.
মসলিন এতই মিহি ছিল যে একটি শাড়ি আংটির ভে: Stories also say muslin was so fine that a sari could pass through a ring or fit inside a matchbox. These stories convey how people understood muslin’s delicacy, although the historical accuracy of each story is difficult to verify separately.
মসলিন শিল্পের পতন: The decline of the muslin industry
ঔপনিবেশিক আমলে বাংলার বস্ত্রশিল্প গভীর প: Bengal’s textile industry underwent profound changes during the colonial period. The East India Company’s commercial control and pressure on artisans, changing markets, and later competition from inexpensive machine-made British cloth together damaged traditional production. Knowledge of spinning muslin’s exceptionally fine yarn and weaving the cloth gradually began to disappear. Important elements of this craft heritage survive in weaving traditions such as jamdani.
১৮৫১ সালে লন্ডনের Great Exhibition-এ ঢাক: Muslin from Dhaka was displayed at London’s Great Exhibition in 1851. Historical muslin preserved in museums still testifies to this craftsmanship.

জিনোম হলো কোনো জীবের প্রায় সম্পূর্ণ বংশগ: A genome is an organism’s nearly complete set of hereditary instructions. Through genome sequencing, researchers read the order of the chemical components of DNA. This information can be used to investigate genetic relationships and characteristics among plants.
-এ প্রকাশিত “Genome sequence of the cult: published “Genome sequence of the cultivated cotton Gossypium arboreum,” in which Li and colleagues sequenced and analysed the genome of a cultivated variety of this species. Alongside genes and evolution, the study investigated traits associated with fibre growth and disease resistance.
গবেষণায় ব্যবহৃত তুলার জাত Shixiya1। এটি: The variety used in the study was Shixiya1. This was not a direct comparative test of phuti karpas against historical Dhakai muslin samples. The study alone therefore does not prove a complete genetic match between recovered cotton and the cotton used in historical muslin.
সাময়িকীতে প্রকাশিত একটি গবেষণায় ফুটি কার: published a study using a convolutional neural network to identify phuti karpas plants from images. The computer attempts to identify a plant from visible features in photographs. Image identification and DNA testing are different methods; the result of one is not a direct substitute for the other.
বাসসের বরাতে দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ডের: According to a Business Standard report citing BSS, more than 300 women have received training in fine spinning through the muslin revival project. The report also describes completion of an order for 500 yards of muslin for international markets. Sustaining the skills of cotton growers, spinners, and weavers, ensuring quality, paying artisans fairly, and training the next generation are important to the initiative’s future.
ঢাকাই মসলিনের গল্প শুধু অতীতের গৌরবের গল: The story of Dhakai muslin is more than past glory. It is a story of the knowledge, creativity, and labour of Bengal’s people, connecting traditional craftsmanship with genome research and artificial intelligence.
